findings.statement: CA9 is first in the convergence ranking. Its Open Targets association with ccRCC is moderate and driven by literature [gene=CA9; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.3088]. It is tractable by antibody, PROTAC and small molecule, with antibody tractability at the advanced clinical level, and the drug layer lists girentuximab (Phase 3) and iodine-124 girentuximab (Phase 2). UniProt places it at the cell membrane, so it is accessible to antibodies and usable for imaging. DepMap shows no ccRCC cell-line dependency, so it is a surface antigen and imaging or biomarker target rather than a functional vulnerability.

CD70 has only a weak prior Open Targets association with ccRCC [gene=CD70; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.0572], but it is tractable by antibody at the advanced clinical level, and the drug layer lists cusatuzumab (Phase 2) and vorsetuzumab mafodotin (Phase 1). UniProt describes a plasma-membrane ligand of CD27. It is not a DepMap dependency in ccRCC lines, so the case rests on an antibody, conjugate or cell-therapy tumour antigen, not on a functional dependency.

EPAS1 (HIF-2 alpha) is an established ccRCC drug target with an approved small molecule, belzutifan. It is the only reviewed gene with a selective ccRCC dependency [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3], with a minority of ccRCC lines dependent [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; frac_ccrcc_dependent=0.208], and it is not common essential.

KDR (VEGFR2) is an established ccRCC drug target among the top Open Targets associations [gene=KDR; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.4566], with approved small molecules such as axitinib and tivozanib. DepMap shows no ccRCC cell-line dependency, consistent with an endothelial, microenvironment-mediated mechanism rather than tumour-cell dependence.

MTOR is an established ccRCC drug target with approved rapalogs. Every ccRCC line depends on it [gene=MTOR; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; frac_ccrcc_dependent=1], but it is flagged common essential, with most other lines dependent too [gene=MTOR; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; frac_all_dependent=0.964], which implies a toxicity risk and a narrow therapeutic window rather than a ccRCC-selective vulnerability.

PBRM1 is a recurrent driver, mutated in about a third of tumours across CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC [gene=PBRM1; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.362], and among the strongest Open Targets associations [gene=PBRM1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.6348]. With no tractability or drug evidence, it is a mechanism and stratification gene rather than a direct drug target.

VHL is the defining ccRCC driver, mutated in close to half of tumours [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.4834], and the top Open Targets association [gene=VHL; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.6466]. VHL loss stabilises HIF and underlies the CA9 and EPAS1 biology. As a loss-of-function driver it is not directly druggable; the therapeutic route runs through HIF-2 alpha.

SCARB1 has a prior Open Targets association with a genetic component [gene=SCARB1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.4049] and predicted tractability, but no drug in the drug layer. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency, so it is an association gene and a weaker target case than its target-profile rank suggests.

NNMT has strong tumour-up expression with a prognostic association, but its Open Targets association is weak [gene=NNMT; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.0598] and no drug is listed. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency, so a biomarker or metabolic-context role is better supported than a target role by the external layer.

ALDOB is second in the convergence ranking because of strong tumour-down expression, replication and prognosis, while its Open Targets association is weak [gene=ALDOB; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.0701] and no drug is listed. Because it is lost in the tumour, it is a diagnostic or prognostic biomarker of the proximal-tubule programme and not a drug target.

PIGR has an Open Targets association with a genetic component [gene=PIGR; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.4532], is lower in tumour than in normal tissue and has no drug, so it is a biomarker candidate rather than a target.

SLC22A8 is strongly down-regulated with a favourable prognostic association. The drug layer lists probenecid and pratosartan, which act on renal transport and are not ccRCC therapies, and its Open Targets association is weak [gene=SLC22A8; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.0662]. It marks loss of the proximal-tubule programme and is not a target.

caveats: Open Targets scores are literature and genetics aggregates and do not imply dependency; top associated genes (VHL, PBRM1, KDM5C, BAP1, SETD2) are mostly loss-of-function drivers without direct drugs.
DepMap measures cell-line-autonomous dependency in ccRCC lines; it cannot capture microenvironmental targets such as KDR or immune and antibody targets such as CD70 and CA9.
Drug stages are reported as returned by Open Targets; the lists are not curated for ccRCC indication, so drugs such as sulthiame and probenecid reflect other uses.
Only the top rows of the convergence ranking were inspected, and STRING interactors were not queried in this run.
